Hi Jonas,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We need to capture a short operational checklist so our legal and ops teams can sign off on the 'no training / no-model-improvement' commitment for the upcoming pilot. High-level asks from our side:

- Confirmation that data sent to Redwood during the pilot will be excluded from model training and model improvement pipelines (not just labeled as 'no-train' but actually blocked downstream).
- A repeatable export path (SFTP or secure API) for all tenant inputs + generated responses at retention interval X (we'll propose 30 days) for archiving.
- Proof points: attestation or evidence we can include with our DPA (audit log extract, subprocessor list, and a short ops runbook).
- Redaction guidance for PII in prompts and any recommended client-side helpers.

Can you send a short, operational checklist (step-by-step) and an example of the artifacts you can provide so we can attach them to the DPA? Procurement wants to see the timeline and any gating items before they issue the PO.

Thanks,

Hi Sana — thanks for the clear list and the spreadsheet. Below is the operational checklist and the artifacts we can commit to for the pilot. I've kept items pragmatic so procurement can see concrete deliverables and timelines.

Operational checklist (Redwood responsibilities):
1) No-training toggle: we will enable an account-level "no-train" flag for Medilink pilot tenants before ingest begins. This flag is enforced at the ingestion layer and prevents any prompts, completions, or telemetry from entering model-improvement pipelines or transfer/export queues used for model training.

2) Evidence bundle (delivered within 3 business days of request):
   - Audit log extract covering ingestion events (JSON lines with timestamps, request id, model id, training-flag) for the requested period.
   - Subprocessor snapshot (CSV) showing active subprocessors and their roles during the pilot window.
   - Ops runbook excerpt (PDF) that describes the toggle, verification steps, and rollback.

3) Export path and cadence:
   - Primary option: Secure SFTP push to Medilink's provisioned host. We will push zipped daily exports (encrypted, AES-256) containing tenant inputs + responses after N days (configurable; default 30).
   - Alternate option: Secure API (mutual TLS) with paginated export endpoints if you prefer pull.

4) Retention & deletion workflow:
   - Default: ephemeral storage for 7 days, then move to short-term export staging for the 30-day retention window.
   - At pilot end or on contract termination we will perform a documented wipe of staging buckets and provide a deletion certificate.

5) PII redaction & client-side helpers:
   - Recommended client-side SDK option: prompt preprocessor that tokenizes and redacts PHI/PII patterns (we'll share a lightweight library and config file).
   - We can also enable built-in server-side redaction rules for common patterns if you want us to handle redactions on ingestion (requires review).

6) Verification & attestation steps prior to PO:
   - Enable no-train flag in test tenant and provide audit log snippet showing flagged requests (within 48 hours).
   - Deliver evidence bundle (see item 2).
   - Provide sample export to your SFTP (small sample) to validate format and keys.

Estimated timeline: enabling the flag and providing a sample export and log snippet: 2 business days after we receive signed SOW. Full evidence bundle: 3 business days. Wipe certificate: 1 business day following wipe.

Attachments we can produce: NO_TRAIN_SOW_v1.pdf (SOW template with acceptance criteria), sample-audit-log.jsonl (redacted), ops-runbook-excerpt.pdf

Let me know if procurement needs any language changes in the SOW. Aditya (cc'd) will run pricing/PO conversation once the scope is confirmed. Kim, please review the attestation wording I'm proposing below and suggest edits.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Head of Product — Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Thanks Jonas — this is a good first pass. A couple of compliance notes and suggested attestation wording: please incorporate before sending anything to procurement.

Compliance notes:
- The "no-train" flag must be honored not only by Redwood's model-improvement pipelines but also by any experimental telemetry consumers (feature flag: exclude-no-train). We'll add a short QA checklist to the runbook showing how we validate that exclusion (unit of measure: request-id sampling).
- Subprocessor snapshot should include effective dates for each subprocessor and a contact for escalation if an auditor needs evidence.
- For international data residency concerns: confirm that the sample export contains an explicit field indicating data location (region tag) so Medilink can validate EU/US residency if needed.

Proposed attestation paragraph (for the SOW / DPA annex):
"Redwood Inference hereby certifies that, for the Pilot Tenant(s) identified in this Statement of Work, Redwood will enforce an account-level 'no-training' flag that prevents the tenant's data from being used for model training, fine-tuning, or any model improvement activity during the pilot period. Redwood will provide an evidence bundle upon request consisting of audit logs, subprocessor records, and export samples, and will execute certified deletion of retained staging data in accordance with the agreed retention schedule."

Two small edits to the operational checklist:
- Specify the encryption standard for exports (AES-256 with key wrap via KMS).
- Add the acceptance test: Medilink will confirm successful ingest and sample export within 48 hours of onboarding the test tenant.

If Sana/Procurement are comfortable, we can send the SOW with the attestation paragraph included and a separate attachment with the QA checklist.

Kim
Kimberly Park
Director, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
